_patient.input_block:
59M, EW EMER. admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to SKILLED NURSING FACILITY
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Septic shock; Retention of urine, unspecified
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Unspecified septicemia
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Unspecified septicemia; Infection and inflammatory reaction due to other internal orthopedic device, implant, and graft; Urinary tract infection, site not specified; Chronic systolic heart failure; Severe sepsis; Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy; Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS); Bipolar disorder, unspecified; Congestive heart failure, unspecified; Thrombocytopenia, unspecified
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Examination of participant in clinical trial; Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
PROCEDURES: Venous catheterization, not elsewhere classified
MEDICATIONS: Tamsulosin 0.4mg PO; Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 1mL IV; Senna 1TAB PO/NG; Neutra-Phos 1PKT PO/NG; Finasteride 5mg PO; Docusate Sodium 100mg PO; 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000mL IV; Ciprofloxacin HCl 500mg PO/NG; Furosemide 60mg PO/NG; Zonisamide 400mg PO; 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV; CefePIME 2g IV; Warfarin 2mg PO/NG; Potassium Chloride 40mEq PO; Phenytoin Sodium Extended 300mg PO; Gabapentin 300mg PO/NG; Miconazole Powder 2% 1Appl TP; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 10mL IV; Carbamazepine Chewable Tabs 300mg PO/NG; Ascorbic Acid 500mg PO/NG; Citalopram 20mg PO/NG; Bag 100mL IV; Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV; Acetaminophen 325-650mg PO/NG; 5% Dextrose 250mL IV DRIP; NORepinephrine 8mg IV DRIP; Quetiapine Fumarate 12.5mg PO/NG; Lidocaine Viscous 2% 20mL PO; Divalproex (DELayed Release) 500mg PO; Azithromycin 250mg PO/NG; Cefpodoxime Proxetil 200mg PO/NG; Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 200mL IV; Vancomycin 1000mg IV; MetRONIDAZOLE (FLagyl) 500mg PO/NG; Aspirin 81mg PO/NG; Bisacodyl 10mg PR; FoLIC Acid 1mg PO/NG; Polyethylene Glycol 17g PO/NG; Multivitamins 1TAB PO/NG
MICROBIOLOGY: MRSA SCREEN: POSITIVE FOR METHICILLIN RESISTANT STAPH AUREUS
SERVICES: MED
WARDS: Emergency Department; Medicine; Medical/Surgical Intensive Care Unit (MICU/SICU)
_patient.note:
[1] The patient presented with septic shock and urinary retention.
[2] The patient was diagnosed with unspecified septicemia, infection and inflammatory reaction due to other internal orthopedic device, implant, and graft, urinary tract infection, chronic systolic heart failure, severe sepsis, epilepsy, unspecified, hypertrophy (benign) of prostate with urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS), bipolar disorder, unspecified, congestive heart failure, unspecified, thrombocytopenia, unspecified, and venous thrombosis and embolism.
[3] The patient has a past medical history of participation in a clinical trial and personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism.
[4] The patient underwent venous catheterization.
[5] The patient was treated with Tamsulosin, Heparin Flush, Senna, Neutra-Phos, Finasteride, Docusate Sodium, 0.9% Sodium Chloride, Ciprofloxacin HCl, Furosemide, Zonisamide, 0.9% Sodium Chloride, CefePIME, Warfarin, Potassium Chloride, Phenytoin Sodium Extended, Gabapentin, Miconazole Powder, Sodium Chloride Flush, Carbamazepine Chewable Tabs, Ascorbic Acid, Citalopram, 5% Dextrose, NORepinephrine, Quetiapine Fumarate, Lidocaine Viscous, Divalproex, Azithromycin, Cefpodoxime Proxetil, Iso-Osmotic Dextrose, Vancomycin, MetRONIDAZOLE, Aspirin, Bisacodyl, FoLIC Acid, Polyethylene Glycol, and Multivitamins.
[6] The patient was administered MRSA SCREEN which was positive for Methicillin Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus.
[7] The patient was admitted to the Emergency Department, Medicine, and Medical/Surgical Intensive Care Unit (MICU/SICU).
[8] The patient was discharged alive to a skilled nursing facility.
